n: Set against the works of the flesh (vv.19–21), inside Paul's argument that those led by the Spirit are not under the law.
Love heads the list; earlier in the chapter Paul says the whole law is fulfilled in love of neighbour.
r: The command Paul quotes in 5:14: love thy neighbour as thyself.
The righteous as a tree bringing forth fruit in his season.
The Spirit resting on the coming Branch, described by its qualities.
The law written in the heart, not on stone.
God puts his spirit within his people and causes them to walk in his ways.
The promise that the Spirit would be poured out on all flesh.
A good tree brings forth good fruit: character shown by what grows.
Fruit comes from abiding in him.
The Spirit of truth would dwell in them.
Peter declares Joel's promise fulfilled at Pentecost.
l: Paul's portrait of love uses two of the same qualities: suffereth long, is kind.

Gal.5.23.ph: against such there is no law
n: The list closes with a direct answer to the dispute over the law in Galatia.
r: Moses, the lawgiver, is called very meek.
When the law is in the heart, there is nothing for it to stand against.
Jesus calls himself meek and lowly in heart.
l: Paul reasons with Felix about temperance.

n: Walking is the Old Testament picture of a way of life.
r: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly.
God's spirit within causes his people to walk in his statutes.

John.1.1.ph: In the beginning was the Word
n: John opens with the first words of Genesis.
r: The same opening: In the beginning.
God speaks and it is so: creation by word.
By the word of the LORD were the heavens made.
l: The same writer's Word of life, heard, seen and handled.
By him were all things created.
The worlds were framed by the word of God.

John.1.3.ph: All things were made by him
r: God created the heaven and the earth.
By the word of the LORD were the heavens made.
l: All things were created by him, and for him.

r: Darkness was upon the face of the deep.
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.

John.1.14.ph: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us
r: Make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.
The glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.

n: Israel had been pictured as God's vine; here Jesus calls himself the true one.
r: A prayer: thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt.
The vineyard of the LORD is the house of Israel; he looked for judgment but found oppression.
God looking for fruit in his vineyard.
John the Baptist: every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down.

John.15.4.ph: Abide in me, and I in you
r: A tree planted by the waters does not cease from yielding fruit.

John.15.5.ph: I am the vine, ye are the branches
r: A tree planted by the rivers of water brings forth fruit.
Roots by the river; leaves stay green in drought.
l: Paul names the fruit: love, joy, peace…

Matt.5.3.ph: Blessed are the poor in spirit
r: The Psalms' first word over a way of life: Blessed.
Good tidings to the meek, binding up the brokenhearted.
l: Jesus reads Isaiah 61 aloud in Nazareth.

Matt.5.5.ph: the meek: for they shall inherit the earth
n: Jesus repeats a line of the Psalms almost word for word.
r: But the meek shall inherit the earth.
l: I am meek and lowly in heart.
Meekness listed as fruit of the Spirit.

r: Who may ascend the hill of the LORD: he that hath clean hands, and a pure heart.
David prays: Create in me a clean heart.

Matt.7.16.ph: Ye shall know them by their fruits
n: Spoken as a test for false prophets.
r: The righteous bring forth fruit in season.
A tree that never ceases from yielding fruit.

Matt.7.17.ph: every good tree bringeth forth good fruit
r: Like a tree planted by the rivers of water.

Matt.7.19.ph: hewn down, and cast into the fire
n: John the Baptist had used the same words earlier.
r: The axe is laid unto the root of the trees.

n: Peter answers the mockers by pointing them to scripture.
r: The passage Peter is about to quote.

Acts.2.17.ph: I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh
n: Where Joel says afterward, Peter says in the last days.
r: I will put my spirit within you.

l: John begins his Gospel with the same words.
The worlds were framed by the word of God.
By him were all things created.

Gen.1.2.ph: the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters
l: Jesus plays on wind and Spirit, one word in Greek.
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
The Beatitudes open the same way.

Ps.1.3.ph: bringeth forth his fruit in his season
l: Jeremiah takes up the same tree by the water.

Ps.51.10.ph: Create in me a clean heart
r: God created: the same Hebrew verb.
l: God promises a new heart and a new spirit.
Blessed are the pure in heart.
Joy as fruit of the Spirit.

Isa.11.1.ph: a Branch shall grow out of his roots
l: He shall be called a Nazarene (see word study).

Isa.11.2.ph: the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him
l: I have put my spirit upon him.
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me.

Isa.53.5.ph: with his stripes we are healed
l: Peter: by whose stripes ye were healed.

n: Part of the promised new covenant.
l: Against such there is no law.

Ezek.36.26.ph: A new heart also will I give you
n: God had made the same promise earlier in Ezekiel.
r: David had prayed for exactly this.
One heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh.
l: Born of water and of the Spirit.

Ezek.36.27.ph: I will put my spirit within you
r: Take not thy holy spirit from me.
l: He dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.

Joel.2.28.ph: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh
